title: The biggest names in AI are backing a new way to opt out of scraping
summary: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic say they will adopt a new standard that publishers can use to opt out of being scraped by AI, as reported earlier by Search Engine Roundtable. With this control, publishers can apply their AI training preferences across multiple AI companies, instead of setting them individually. The shared "policy token" signal […]
title_es: OpenAI, Google y Microsoft acuerdan estándar para opt-out de scraping
bajada: Las cuatro principales compañías de IA adoptarán un nuevo estándar que permite a los publicadores optar por no ser incluidos en entrenamientos de IA mediante un único token de política. Esta iniciativa simplifica el control sobre datos en múltiples plataformas simultáneamente.
bajada_en: The four major AI companies will adopt a new standard allowing publishers to opt out of AI training across multiple platforms with a single policy token. This initiative simplifies data control across multiple AI platforms simultaneously.

title: An AI Agent Injected Drugs Into a Live Mouse’s Brain
summary: A biotech startup let an agent choose a gene therapy and successfully inject the treatment, offering a startling glimpse of the future of research labs.
title_es: Agente de IA realiza inyección de terapia génica en ratón vivo
bajada: Un startup de biotech permitió que un agente de IA seleccionara y aplicara una terapia génica en un ratón vivo, marcando un paso importante en la automatización de investigación científica. Este avance demuestra el potencial de IA en experimentación biomédica de precisión.
bajada_en: A biotech startup allowed an AI agent to select and administer gene therapy to a live mouse, marking a significant step in scientific research automation. This advance demonstrates AI's potential in precision biomedical experimentation.

title: Google’s satellite AI server transmits its first response to Earth
summary: Google's AI chip-equipped satellite has generated its first response from space. In a blog post on Friday, Google says it successfully booted up the satellite's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), allowing the on-board Gemma 4 model to follow through on a prompt to create a haiku about being in space: Blue marble below Data streams in […]
title_es: Google ejecuta IA en satélite y recibe primera respuesta desde el espacio
bajada: Google logró ejecutar exitosamente sus TPUs y el modelo Gemma 4 en un satélite equipado con chips de IA, demostrando capacidades de procesamiento en órbita. Este hito abre posibilidades para aplicaciones de IA distribuidas y procesamiento en ubicaciones remotas.
bajada_en: Google successfully executed its TPUs and Gemma 4 model on an AI-equipped satellite, demonstrating processing capabilities in orbit. This milestone opens possibilities for distributed AI applications and processing in remote locations.

title: Meta Built Humanoid Prototype With Chinese Startup To Ramp Up Robotics Push
summary: Meta Platformshas built a prototype humanoid with Chinese robotics company Fourier and is already working on a second version, as the social media giant steps up efforts to develop robots for people’s homes, according to people familiar with the initiative.Meta and Fourier built the roughly 106-pound humanoid, known internally as Max, in just three months. The goal was to help Meta develop a more polished future product at its robotics arm that it could eventually release as a product, one of the people said, adding that no launch target had been set.
title_es: Meta desarrolla prototipo de robot humanoide con startup china Fourier
bajada: Meta construyó en tres meses un prototipo humanoide de 48 kg llamado Max junto con Fourier Intelligence, acelerando su estrategia en robótica doméstica. La compañía ya trabaja en una segunda versión aunque sin fecha de lanzamiento confirmada.
bajada_en: Meta built a 48-kg humanoid prototype called Max in just three months with Fourier Intelligence, accelerating its home robotics strategy. The company is already working on a second version, though no confirmed launch date has been set.

title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
summary: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
title_es: Extensión de Anthropic en Cursor comprometida durante 12 horas
bajada: La extensión de VS Code de Anthropic en Cursor fue hackeada y comprometida por casi medio día, aunque aún se desconoce cómo los atacantes obtuvieron acceso a la cuenta verificada. El incidente destaca vulnerabilidades en la cadena de distribución de herramientas de desarrollo.
bajada_en: Anthropic's VS Code extension on Cursor was compromised for nearly 12 hours, though attackers' method of accessing the verified account remains unknown. The incident highlights vulnerabilities in the developer tools supply chain.

title: Judge allows NAACP lawsuit over xAI data center pollution to move forward
summary: An NAACP lawsuit accuses the SpaceX-owned AI company of violating the Clean Air Act.
title_es: Demanda de NAACP contra xAI por contaminación del data center avanza
bajada: Un juez permitió que prosiga la demanda de la NAACP contra xAI acusándola de violar la Ley de Aire Limpio por contaminación de su data center. El caso refleja crecientes preocupaciones sobre el impacto ambiental de la infraestructura de IA a gran escala.
bajada_en: A judge allowed an NAACP lawsuit against xAI to proceed, accusing the company of violating the Clean Air Act due to data center pollution. The case reflects growing concerns about the environmental impact of large-scale AI infrastructure.

title: Spooky New Infostealer Malware Uses AI to ‘Autodox’ Victims
summary: Named “Volta-Autodoxer,” the recently uncovered malware uses AI tools to collect troves of data about victims, from login credentials and credit card numbers to Discord sessions and UberEats receipts.
title_es: Malware Volta-Autodoxer usa IA para recopilar datos de víctimas
bajada: Se descubrió un nuevo malware infostealer llamado Volta-Autodoxer que utiliza herramientas de IA para automatizar la recopilación masiva de datos personales, desde credenciales hasta registros de sesiones. El hallazgo evidencia la evolución de amenazas cibernéticas mediante IA.
bajada_en: A new infostealer malware called Volta-Autodoxer uses AI tools to automate mass collection of personal data, from credentials to session logs. The discovery highlights evolving cyber threats leveraging AI.

title: OpenAI reportedly lowers funding target for new round
summary: OpenAI’s latest funding round doesn't seem to be living up to expectations.

bajada: La última ronda de financiación de OpenAI no está alcanzando las expectativas iniciales, lo que llevó a la compañía a reducir su objetivo de captación. El cambio sugiere desafíos en la valoración o condiciones de inversión más restrictivas.

title: WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments
summary:
arXiv:2610.37786v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Web agents require diverse, executable, and resettable website environments for reproducible training and evaluation. Human-assisted mirrors demand per-site engineering, while generative construction can diverge from specified real websites. Capture-and-replay preserves observations, with interaction coverage constrained by captured content and replay capabilities.
  We present WebAnything, a fully automated framework that reconstructs source-grounded, reusable Web environments from real URLs without per-site manual implementation or repair after initial setup and authorization. An Explorer-Builder collects browser-observable structures, resources, and interaction outcomes; an independent verifier checks frozen candidates and guides local repair or targeted source recapture.
  We construct 244 website artifacts across 14 application domains and 53 categories, supporting 12,984 executed and accepted tasks. Compared with human-assisted WebHarbor, WebAnything achieves higher aggregate scores on three fidelity metrics, with 12 wins, two ties, and no losses in a blind audit. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B on 5,856 interaction trajectories improves REAL success by 9.9 percentage points, Odysseys-Easy Rubric Avg and Task Avg by 6.25 and 6.32 percentage points, and WebArena-Verified Overall success by 13.33 percentage points under the fixed harness. Code: https://github.com/china-qijizhifeng/Web-Anything
title_es: WebAnything: framework para crear ambientes web escalables para agentes
bajada: WebAnything es un framework que reconstruye automáticamente ambientes web ejecutables desde URLs reales sin intervención manual por sitio. El sistema permite entrenar y evaluar agentes web sobre 244 artefactos de sitios reales, mejorando la reproducibilidad.
bajada_en: WebAnything is a framework that automatically reconstructs executable web environments from real URLs without per-site manual work. The system enables training and evaluating web agents on 244 real website artifacts, improving reproducibility.

title: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery
summary:
arXiv:2610.37739v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown increasing promise in research-level problem solving, yet a comprehensive collection of such problems is still missing, and evaluating them on research-level problems remains challenging. We introduce OpenFrontiers, a cross-disciplinary resource that combines a structured corpus of open research problems with a retrospective benchmark of recently resolved problems in mathematics. The corpus records problem statements, context, progress, and other information for 12,151 problems. The benchmark contains 200 problems, 110 resolved in 2026 and 90 still open, each with a Lean~4 statement checked by automated probes and two independent reviews; a subset HQ-50 further filters based on quality score, etc. Our evaluation protocol grades formal proofs with two independent checkers in an isolated sandbox under closed-book, frozen-retrieval, and live-web conditions. Evaluating seven LLM agents on the HQ-50 subset under a standardized budget, we find that closed-book rediscovery is rare, at most 7 of 40 resolved problems, whereas live-web success mostly reflects retrieval of published solutions. By linking a broad research-problem corpus to a formally graded evaluation subset with documented solutions, OpenFrontiers provides a foundation for measuring research-level rediscovery and studying progress toward solving currently open scientific problems. The dataset and benchmark could be found in https://huggingface.co/collections/FlippyDora/openfrontiers.
title_es: OpenFrontiers: benchmark de problemas abiertos en investigación científica
bajada: OpenFrontiers combina un corpus de 12,151 problemas de investigación abiertos con un benchmark retrospectivo de 200 problemas resueltos en matemáticas. El recurso permite evaluar agentes LLM en resolución de problemas científicos formalizados en Lean 4.
bajada_en: OpenFrontiers combines a corpus of 12,151 open research problems with a retrospective benchmark of 200 solved math problems. The resource enables evaluating LLM agents on scientific problem-solving formalized in Lean 4.

title: ThinkJev: One Thought, Every Budget for Calibrated Typed Decisions
summary:
arXiv:2610.37732v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many uses of language models end in a typed decision: a choice among a closed set of options, whose probabilities code can act on. Reading those probabilities from one forward pass is fast but often wrong on decisions that take several steps, such as arithmetic, counting, and date comparison. Letting the model think first fixes most of these errors, but costs seconds per decision instead of milliseconds. To pay for thinking only where it helps, ThinkJev builds a fast and a slow system from one open hybrid-thinking model that can answer directly or after a thought. System 1 reads the model's probabilities for the option letters when it answers directly; System 2 reads the same letters after the model has thought on the same cached prompt, so escalating repeats no work and both systems give probabilities over the same options. Because the letters can be read after any number of thought tokens, one sampled thought also gives the answer under every thinking budget. Without training, ThinkJev lets System 1 answer alone only where a statistical test on labeled dev data guarantees that its accepted answers stay under a target error rate. At a 5% target, Qwen3.5-27B answers 24.5% of 8359 test decisions this way with a realized error of 3.9% (Qwen3.5-4B and 9B: 6.5% and 0.0%). For the rest, stopping each thought as soon as its answer is confident reaches 81.6% accuracy, against 82.7% for always thinking, with 72% of the thought tokens. Choosing when to think from System 1's confidence alone saves less, because the decisions System 1 is least sure of are often not the ones thinking fixes. On the public items of JevBench, an independent benchmark of typed-decision services, Qwen3.5-27B thinks on 29.4% and is not distinguishable in accuracy from the two thinking APIs listed (exploratory). Code and data generators are available at https://github.com/ding-xiaolu/ThinkJev.
title_es: ThinkJev: modelo híbrido que calibra razonamiento por presupuesto computacional
bajada: ThinkJev es un método que construye sistemas rápido y lento desde un único modelo que puede responder directamente o después de razonar, ajustando el coste computacional dinámicamente. La técnica permite decisiones tipadas precisas sin sacrificar velocidad en casos simples.
bajada_en: ThinkJev is a method building fast and slow systems from a single model that can answer directly or after reasoning, dynamically adjusting computational cost. The technique enables precise typed decisions without sacrificing speed on simple cases.

title: Are there fundamental repeating patterns in ML techniques across modalities (text, image, audio) that let us group them? [R]
summary: I’ve been noticing that a lot of techniques seem to repeat across modalities with just a different name.For example, tokenisation, masking (MLM / MAE / audio masking), diffusion, next-token / next-frame prediction, etc.Is there an existing taxonomy or mental model that groups ML techniques by their underlying pattern rather than by modality (NLP / vision / audio)?This will help me to group the research papers and then make reference to work already done in that domainsubmitted by/u/OkCampaign8400[link][comments]
title_es: Discusión sobre patrones fundamentales de técnicas ML entre modalidades
bajada: Un usuario plantea si existen patrones recurrentes en técnicas de ML que trascienden modalidades (texto, imagen, audio) para crear una taxonomía unificada. La pregunta busca herramientas conceptuales para entender similitudes en tokenización, masking y predicción.
bajada_en: A user questions whether fundamental patterns in ML techniques transcend modalities (text, image, audio) to create a unified taxonomy. The question seeks conceptual tools to understand similarities in tokenization, masking, and prediction.
